text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Interior and legal politicians of the ruling coalition agree to comprehensive penal law reform including tougher sentences for sex offenders.
- Coalition challenges opposition Social Democrats (SPD) over corporate tax ahead of parliament debate on government's annual economic report on Thursday.
- General secretary of Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) Bernd Protzner criticises new spelling laws.
- Two freight trains crash in Frankfurt, but catastrophe narroly avoided.
- German business is mainly behind tax plans of Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
- Economic growth slowed more in the former east than the west last year to just two percent.
HANDELSBLATT
- Economic recovery cames to a standstill at turn of the year, the Bundesbank and the German Institue for Economic research say.
- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind criticises Chancellor Helmut Kohl's analysis on Europe.
- Imposing withholding tax on interest income does not violate Germany's constitution, the country's finance court decides.
- Hans-Peter Stihl, president of German Chambers of Industry and Commerce, says he is against an increase in value-added tax to finance planned tax and pension reforms.
- SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Cabinet decides to reduce transition payments for former ministers and state secretaries.

- Four former East German intelligence officers go on trial for sheltering some of West Germany's most wanted guerrillas and argue they had done a good deed by preventing potential attacks in the West.
- CSU's Protzner argues against new spelling laws.
- German finance court decides impossing witholding tax on interest income does not violate constitution.
DIE WELT
- Coalition agrees on tougher sentences for sex criminals.
- Britain's Rifkind triggers irritation in Bonn on visit with criticism of Europe and the policies of Kohl.
- Bundesbank says record unemployment and weak growth could threaten entry into planned currency union.
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer rejects attacks on health reform plans.
